key_insight: MANTA lets a multi-agent system adapt its communication topology during inference, so the collaboration structure can self-evolve when the current setup is no longer effective.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical way to improve multi-agent AI performance without changing the task interface or agent budget, by updating roles, links, ordering, visibility, and validation pathways on the fly.
method: Initialize a task-conditioned topology from prior structural experience before execution.
Monitor collaboration traces during deployment and trigger bounded structural updates when coordination degrades.
Adapt network structure while preserving the existing agent set and task interface.
evidence_signal: The paper evaluates MANTA on five benchmarks and reports the best average score of 74.0, beating the strongest baseline by 5.8 points and achieving the top result on PlanCraft.
watch_item: Dynamic topology updates may add complexity in control, debugging, and stability, so bounded update rules and reliable monitoring are critical.
paper_title: MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems
